**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Attach the cap warning to its account provider**

When a Mercury account reaches the 100-page cap, this warning records only the family and a provider account ID in free-form metadata even though `mercury_account.account_provider` is available. Consequently `DebugLogEntry` leaves its `account_provider_id` (and associated `account_id`) null, so the support UI cannot filter or trace this truncation incident to the affected linked connection; pass the account provider to `capture`.

**Propagate failed transaction imports to the sync.** When a later page returns a non-hash response, `fetch_account_transactions` discards the accumulated pages and `fetch_and_store_transactions` returns a failure result. `MercuryItem::Syncer#perform_sync` ignores that result, so `Sync#perform` reaches `complete!` and advances `last_synced_at`. The next import can then start at `last_synced_at - 7.days`, which can exclude transactions from the failed window. The pre-change single request already had the same failure-result handling. Pagination materially worsens the behavior because earlier pages are also discarded when a later page fails. Propagate a failed import through the syncer so the sync fails and the next retry retains the original window.
Suggested fix
```diff - mercury_item.import_latest_mercury_data + import_result = mercury_item.import_latest_mercury_data + unless import_result[:success] + raise StandardError, "Mercury import failed: #{import_result[:error] || import_result.inspect}" + end ```

** Major** · **Data Integrity & Integration** · **Heavy lift** **Do not complete a truncated import at the page cap.** If the window contains more than 100,000 transactions, this returns a successful partial result. Mercury defaults to descending order, so older transactions can remain unfetched. After sync completion, the seven-day window can exclude those transactions permanently. ([docs.mercury.com](https://docs.mercury.com/reference/listaccounttransactions?utm_source=openai)) Resume from a persisted checkpoint or fetch the remaining range before completing the sync. Ensure the syncer also treats an incomplete import as incomplete.

Thanks @jjmata. Addressed the open Codex finding in cde1d8f7: the page-cap warning now passes `account_provider`, so the debug log entry is linked to the affected connection (test added: red without the change, green with it).

On the two CodeRabbit comments (checkpointed imports, and propagating a failed import so the sync does not advance `last_synced_at`): the syncer already ignored a failed result before this PR, with the single request. With pagination there are more requests, so that path is hit more often, and pages that were already fetched are dropped when a later page fails. The 100-page cap (100,000 transactions) is only a safety bound. It now logs a warning; before, the import silently stopped after the first page. Fixing the failure handling means changing `MercuryItem::Syncer`, so it is left out of this PR to keep it small. If you would rather have it here, I can add it to this PR, or open a follow-up issue.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

No, @jjmata, it was not tested against a live Mercury account. The coverage is unit tests in `MercuryItem::ImporterTest` with stubbed provider responses: an account with 1002 transactions fetched in two requests (offsets 0 and 1000), and a short first page fetched with one request. The page size of 1000 comes from Mercury's list-account-transactions reference, not from a real response, so the multi-page path has not been checked against Mercury's API. If someone with a Mercury account can run a sync on an account with more than 1000 transactions in the window, I'm happy to fix anything it turns up.
